name: MIRIX
version: 0.1.0 (pyproject.toml; HEAD = merge of PR #139, 2026-08-20; still main HEAD on 2026-10-11)
one_line: Letta-derived multi-agent memory server: a meta memory manager LLM routes each input batch to up to five typed memory-manager agents (core, episodic, semantic, resource, knowledge vault; procedural is produced by a separate skill-distillation path), stored in PostgreSQL with full-text search and pgvector, read via LLM topic extraction then per-type retrieval.

locomo.protocol: Paper Table 2: gpt-4.1-mini backbone (write agents and reader), GPT-4.1 LLM judge, adversarial category excluded (cat 1-4, 1,540 q), mean of 3 runs (83.98 / 87.34 / 84.82); per category single-hop 85.11, multi-hop 83.70, open-domain 65.62, temporal 88.39; Full-Context 87.52 under same setup
locomo.source: MIRIX paper arXiv 2507.07957, Section 4.3, Table 2 and Appendix A Table 3

locomo.protocol: Vendor graph-revision branch PR #123 (merged 2026-04-07 into the then 'graph-revision' branch): LLM judge on 1,540 q; reader/judge not stated in PR body; baseline 0.5429, 0.5734 with MIRIX_ENABLE_GRAPH_MEMORY on. The vendor's own later RESULTS.md lists every run before 2026-08-04 as not quotable (gold answers in prompts, shared namespaces).
locomo.source: github.com/Mirix-AI/MIRIX/pull/123 body; evals/RESULTS.md section 0 on branch graph_revision (4dd31c7)

locomo.score: 89.3 mean with graph (89.03 / 89.61); 85.2 mean without graph (85.71 / 84.74)
locomo.protocol: Vendor RESULTS.md on branch graph_revision (not main): same-store four-arm ablation, cat 1-4 = 1,540 q, decontaminated prompts, gpt-4.1-mini ingest agents and answerer (temperature 0, seed 42), gpt-4o-mini judge (single call), ada-002 embeddings, MIRIX_GRAPH_VERSION=v7.23, Neo4j graph; 2 runs per arm; vendor states a QA re-run noise floor of 9-15 questions

arch.product.t: Self-hosted FastAPI server (port 8531) plus React dashboard and Python SDK (mirix-client); three tiers client SDK -> REST -> AsyncServer -> MetaAgent with typed sub-agents. Forked from Letta (agent loop, blocks, tool execution). The screen-capture desktop app from the paper is not in this repo.

arch.truth.t: Derived typed rows are the de facto truth: raw turns are not kept for retrieval by default. Raw turns go to a Conversation Message Store only when a session_id is supplied (used solely for skill distillation, pruned 30 days after distillation); agent in-context messages are cleared after each memory update (CLEAR_HISTORY_AFTER_MEMORY_UPDATE=true), with the last 5 sessions' raw messages kept detached for the distiller (MESSAGE_RETAIN_LAST_N_SESSIONS=5).

arch.stores.t: PostgreSQL + pgvector (one table per memory type: block, episodic_memory, semantic_memory, procedural_memory, resource_memory, knowledge_vault, plus raw_memory, conversation_message, skill_experience, agent_trigger_state); optional Redis Stack as search cache (MIRIX_REDIS_ENABLED default false); SQLite fallback.

arch.graphdb.t: No graph store on main. A Neo4j graph (v7: sparse anchor nodes linking to Postgres episodic/semantic row refs, default off via MIRIX_ENABLE_GRAPH_MEMORY) exists only on branches graph_revision (open PR #130) and graph_v7.1_clean.
arch.graphdb.e: grep for neo4j/entity_node in mirix/ on main returns nothing [read]; docs/graph_memory_v7/README.md and evals/RESULTS.md on graph_revision [doc]; PR #123, #130 [doc]

arch.scope.t: Organisation -> client (API key) -> user; every row carries organization_id, user_id, client_id and a filter_tags JSON with scope = client.write_scope; reads filter by client.read_scopes plus arbitrary filter_tags (GIN-indexed).

write.entry.t: POST /memory/add (queued) and POST /memory/add_sync (blocking); messages are role-prefixed text ([USER]/[ASSISTANT]/[TOOL]); optional session_id, session_tag (conversation|task), occurred_at, filter_tags, chaining flag. Also POST /memory/raw for unprocessed task context.

write.receipt.t: /memory/add returns status 'queued' after put_messages; default queue is an in-process asyncio memory queue (QUEUE_TYPE=memory, 1 worker), so a crash loses unprocessed batches. Kafka (protobuf or JSON, mTLS) is opt-in. Only the optional Conversation Message Store write is durable before return.

write.roles.t: All roles go to the meta memory manager as one prefixed text blob; the LLM decides what to keep. Episodic rows carry an 'actor' field (user or assistant). session_tag='task' suppresses all inline extraction (skill-only); 'conversation' never feeds skills.

write.firewall.t: not found: no injection or poisoning filter on the write path; the meta prompt even asks agents to over-include memory types when unsure.

write.governance.t: Knowledge Vault deliberately stores credentials with a sensitivity label; 'high' items are hidden from non-vault agents' prompts, but secret_value is a plain String column (no encryption found) and GET /memory/search returns secret_value with no sensitivity filter. Raw task memories have a 14-day TTL job and distilled transcripts a 30-day prune, but the TTL job is not scheduled in-repo (operator cron or POST /memory/raw/cleanup). No consent or redaction.

segment.unit.t: One call to /memory/add = one batch; the whole batch is one meta-agent step. The paper app accumulates 20 inputs (TEMPORARY_MESSAGE_LIMIT) before absorbing; the LoCoMo harness sends one full session per add.

segment.rule.t: Caller-defined; no server-side boundary detection. Episodic agent itself chooses insert (new topic) versus merge (same topic continues) per batch. MAB harness uses a 4,096-token sentence-aware chunker.

segment.measured.t: not found on main: per-session add timings are logged by the harness but no published counts of calls or units on LoCoMo. The graph_revision RESULTS.md reports ingest time only (12.8 s/chunk flat, 61.6 s/chunk with graph).

extract.calls.t: Per batch: 1 topic-extraction call (meta agent, step 0) + 1 meta-manager call choosing memory types + 1 call per selected sub-agent run concurrently via asyncio.gather (up to 5), more if chaining or a tool failure triggers a retry. With chaining=False (LoCoMo harness) roughly 3-7 LLM calls per session. Paper: 'one to the meta memory manager and between zero and six to the other memory managers'.

extract.facts.t: Semantic memory holds concept/person/place entries (name, summary, details, source), not atomic facts; Knowledge Vault holds static reference values (caption + secret_value).

extract.episode.t: Episodic events with event_type, summary, verbose details, actor, occurred_at; the agent is told to make one comprehensive call per batch and to merge into an existing event when the topic continues.

extract.dates.t: occurred_at is LLM-produced per event unless the API occurred_at override is passed; the LoCoMo harness prepends instructions to resolve relative dates ('last year' -> 2022) into the text, so absolute dates are prompt-driven, not code-driven.

extract.neighbours.t: Each sub-agent's system prompt is rebuilt with BM25-retrieved memories for the batch topics: its own type with row IDs (for merge/replace) and other types without IDs, MAX_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT_IN_SYSTEM=10 per list (prompt text still says 50). Episodic entries show summary plus details length only.

extract.failure.t: Tool failure injects a 'function call failed' heartbeat and lets the agent retry (chaining); sub-agents run with return_exceptions, so siblings finish and keep their writes, then one failure raises RuntimeError for the whole trigger_memory_update. Context overflow triggers up to 3 summariser retries. Queue has no dead-letter in memory mode.

graph.entities.t: No entity extraction on main; semantic-memory entries named after people/places act as implicit entity cards.

graph.resolution.t: not found on main (semantic dedup is exact name+summary+details equality).

graph.edges.t: not found on main; anchor/memory-ref edges only on the graph_revision branch.

time.fields.t: Episodic occurred_at plus created_at and last_modify {timestamp, operation}; other types have created_at/last_modify only. No valid-from/valid-to.

time.update.t: LLM-driven destructive edits: episodic merge overwrites summary/details; replace deletes rows and inserts new ones; semantic/resource/vault update tools overwrite. No history kept beyond last_modify. Auto-dream (POST /memory/auto_dream, operator-invoked for non-procedural modes) resolves stale/conflicting entries, told to keep both and note the discrepancy when unsure.

time.dedup.t: Semantic, resource and vault inserts skip exact duplicates among up to 1,000 existing items, but the check is filtered by the batch's filter_tags (which carry session_id), so cross-session duplicates can slip (inferred); the meta agent's duplicate memory_types are de-duplicated; otherwise dedup relies on the LLM and on auto-dream consolidation.

derive.session.t: not found as a stored layer; agents' own in-context histories are summarised at 75% context pressure (keep last 5 messages), which is working-memory hygiene, not a retrievable summary.

derive.profile.t: Core memory blocks 'human' and 'persona' (5,000-char limit each) maintained by the core memory agent with append/rewrite tools; overflow returns an error telling the agent to condense to about 50%. Always injected whole into every agent prompt.

derive.entity.t: Semantic memory entries about people/organisations serve as entity summaries (no dedicated layer).

derive.background.t: Auto-dream consolidation agent per mode (core, episodic, semantic, resource, knowledge, experience = episodic+semantic+knowledge jointly; up to 500 items per type); procedural mode is session distillation plus skill evolution, auto-scheduled fire-and-forget every 5 sealed 'task' sessions (SKILL_TRIGGER_SESSION_THRESHOLD) under a Postgres advisory lock; other modes are invoked by API. Reflexion and background agents exist but are off (WITH_REFLEXION_AGENT=False).

derive.forget.t: No decay scoring. Raw task memories can be hard-deleted after 14 days by a job that the operator must schedule (or call POST /memory/raw/cleanup); distilled conversation transcripts are pruned after 30 days at the end of each procedural dream; otherwise deletion only via LLM replace tools, auto-dream, skill soft-delete or API.

index.embed.t: Configurable per agent (README example Google text-embedding-004, 768-d; eval config names OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1536-d, but the OpenAI path builds llama_index OpenAIEmbedding without a model argument, so the library default ada-002 is used); vectors zero-padded to MAX_EMBEDDING_DIM=4096. Episodic insert embeds both details and summary (2 embedding calls per event). BUILD_EMBEDDINGS_FOR_MEMORY can switch embedding off.
index.embed.e: README.md:52-59 [doc]; evals/configs/0201c.yaml:18-23 [read]; mirix/embeddings.py:488-497 [read]; mirix/constants.py:13, 299 [read]; mirix/services/episodic_memory_manager.py:556-566 [read]; evals/RESULTS.md section 1.3 on graph_revision [doc]

index.lexical.t: PostgreSQL to_tsvector('english') with ts_rank_cd; tsquery adds prefix matching (word:*) and tries AND first, then OR for recall. Only episodic_memory has GIN full-text indexes (summary, details, combined); other types compute to_tsvector at query time without an index. Redis Search text index when cache on; in-memory rank_bm25 on SQLite.

index.vector.t: pgvector columns per text field (episodic details/summary; semantic name/summary/details; vault caption); no ANN index declared (GIN only), so vector search is a scan; 4,096-d padding exceeds pgvector's HNSW dimension cap (inferred). Redis vector index when cache on.

read.rewrite.t: Active retrieval: an LLM call with forced tool update_topic_and_time turns the conversation into ';'-separated topics plus a temporal phrase; topics become the BM25 query. Runs on the first agent's main llm_config; optional local Ollama model for topic extraction (no temporal).

read.analysis.t: Temporal expression parsed by a rule-based parser (today, yesterday, last N days/weeks/months, this month ...) into a date range relative to wall-clock now in the user's timezone (not the conversation's date); explicit start/end dates override.

read.legs.t: /memory/retrieve/conversation: per type, BM25 only (search_method hard-coded 'bm25'), limit 10 per type: episodic recent + relevant, semantic, resource, procedural, knowledge vault captions, plus all core blocks; run sequentially. /memory/search defaults to embedding (procedural: hybrid BM25+embedding RRF k=60) and runs all types concurrently.

read.temporal.t: Date range filter on episodic occurred_at only (other types unfiltered).

rank.fusion.t: No cross-type fusion: results stay grouped per memory type. Within procedural, RRF (k=60) fuses BM25 and embedding with 2x over-fetch per lane.

rank.rerank.t: not found on main (a MIRIX_GRAPH_RERANK flag exists only on graph_revision).
rank.rerank.e: code search [read]; evals/RESULTS.md section 1.1 on graph_revision [doc]

rank.gate.t: Optional similarity_threshold on embedding search; the memory prompt tells the model that empty sections mean no relevant memory. No abstain gate.

rank.agentic.t: Chat agent has search_in_memory / list_memory_within_timerange tools; the LoCoMo harness answer agent (gpt-4.1-mini) gets the preliminary retrieval then up to 5 search_memory rounds (default embedding, limit raised to 15).

answer.shape.t: Typed XML sections in the system prompt: current time, <keywords>, <core_memory>, <episodic_memory> recent and relevant (timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)'), <knowledge_vault>, <semantic_memory>, <resource_memory>, each with 'k out of N items'; procedural never injected. LoCoMo harness flattens summaries/captions with timestamps into one block.

answer.size.t: not found: no published tokens per question. Bounded by design at about 50-60 short lines (10 per list) plus up to 10,000 chars of core blocks (inferred); the harness records per-question token usage locally.

answer.prompt.t: Harness answer agent is told to verify results, search both episodic and semantic, aggregate lists, stop after 2-3 searches, say 'unknown' only after three failed searches, and otherwise guess. Its search and answer-format examples are LoCoMo-specific (names and gold-style answers), and its check_raw_item tool relies on a raw_input_id that main never returns.

eval.best.t: 85.38 LoCoMo (cat 1-4), vendor paper, gpt-4.1-mini, mean of 3 runs, below its own Full-Context 87.52. The vendor's later graph_revision RESULTS.md reports a same-store ablation of 85.2 (flat) and 89.3 (with Neo4j graph) means over 2 runs each, gpt-4o-mini judge; its earlier PR #123 figures (54.29 -> 57.34) are flagged by the vendor as unquotable.
eval.best.e: arXiv 2507.07957 Tables 2-3 [doc]; evals/RESULTS.md sections 0-2 on graph_revision [doc]; PR #123 [doc]

eval.outside.t: No independent reproduction found in repo or paper; the task note attributes an 85.38 run to the HyperMem authors, which could not be verified here (same number as the vendor paper, so probably a citation, not a rerun).

eval.models.t: Paper: gpt-4.1-mini writer and reader, GPT-4.1 judge. Repo harness: gpt-4.1-mini memory agents, gpt-4.1-mini topic extraction (the config's gpt-4.1-nano topic_extraction_llm_config key is not read anywhere in mirix/), ada-002 embeddings in practice (config names text-embedding-3-small), gpt-4.1-mini answer agent, gpt-4o-mini judge (generous Mem0-style prompt). Judges differ between paper and repo.

Main's harness injects date-resolution instructions into each ingested session, overrides the episodic/meta/semantic prompts with LoCoMo-tuned ones (evals/prompts/0201a) and gives the reader LoCoMo-specific few-shot answers plus up to 5 agentic searches; cat 5 dropped (no 'answer' key). The vendor's own RESULTS.md says all runs before 2026-08-04 saw gold answers in prompts.

cost.write.t: About 3-7 LLM calls per session with chaining off: roughly 800-1,900 calls for 272 sessions, plus 2 embedding calls per episodic event and more per semantic/vault row (inferred from code path); each call carries a 650-1,300-word agent prompt plus retrieved memory lists. Vendor graph branch: 12.8 s/chunk flat ingest versus 61.6 s with graph.
cost.write.e: mirix/agent/agent.py:1657-1699 [read]; memory_tools.py:1995-2012 [read]; prompt word counts via wc [read]; evals/RESULTS.md section 2.1 on graph_revision [doc]; inferred

cost.read.t: 1 topic-extraction LLM call per /retrieve/conversation plus DB queries (BM25); harness adds 1-6 answer-agent calls with search rounds.

cost.where.t: Hosted LLMs by default (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Azure etc. via llm_api); optional local Ollama for topic extraction only.

trust.provenance.t: Rows record agent_id, client_id, user_id, filter_tags (scope, session_id, session_tag), last_modify operation; semantic/vault have a free-text 'source'. No link from a derived memory row to source turns or message IDs; only skill experiences carry an evidence quote and experience-to-skill lineage (influenced_skill_ids).

trust.erasure.t: DELETE /users/{user_id}/memories hard-deletes memories, messages, blocks, conversation transcripts and skill experiences for a user and clears Redis keys, with an org tenant guard that answers 404 for foreign users; per-item deletes per type; per-client delete.

trust.auth.t: X-API-Key (SHA-256 hashed at rest, constant-time compare) or dashboard JWT, but the key is optional: get_client_and_org accepts a bare x-client-id / x-org-id header with no secret on memory endpoints, and DELETE /users/{user_id} (soft delete) takes no credential at all.

trust.sharing.t: Scopes let multiple clients write to their write_scope and read a list of read_scopes for the same user; agents inside a meta agent share one store. Gaps: the retrieve path queries knowledge_vault without filter_tags, scopes or sensitivity, and agent-prompt retrieval passes no scopes.

extras.t: One LLM call classifies each batch into memory types and fans out to typed manager agents concurrently (asyncio.gather), each with a narrow toolset and type-specific prompt.
'task' sessions skip all inline extraction and only feed skill distillation every 5 sessions; 'conversation' sessions never produce skills.

Procedural memory as versioned skills (name, description, instructions, triggers, examples, version) with an edit budget and size gates; sealed sessions distilled into worth_learning / worth_avoiding experiences that evolve skills.
Offline agent reviews one or more memory types, merges duplicates and resolves stale entries; dry_run supported.

Screen-monitor prompt set and a TemporaryMessageAccumulator (20 inputs, async Gemini file upload, image cleanup) exist, but the accumulator is not wired into the server; the paper's 1 fps screenshot app with >0.99 similarity skip is outside this repo.
Optional Redis Stack mirror with text and vector indexes queried before PostgreSQL; 1-hour TTL.
Opt-in Kafka transport (protobuf or JSON, mTLS) with user_id-hash partitioned workers.
MCP client (stdio, Gmail) with a tool registry/marketplace and sandboxed user-defined tools for the chat agent; MIRIX does not expose its own memory as an MCP server.

extras.param: post-update context wipe with last-edit echo
extras.t: After each memory update a non-chat agent's in-context history is reset to its system message, and the most recently edited item (episodic event or skill) is shown back so the next batch still sees what changed.

Procedural trigger counts sealed sessions against a persisted cursor (agent_trigger_state) under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so restarts and multiple workers fire exactly once per window; dream runs also take a Postgres advisory lock per (user, org).

Each sealed session is distilled in parallel with a head+tail transcript cap (80,000 chars per session, 8,000 per turn); failed sessions are not marked distilled so they retry, and pending experiences from a failed evolution are drained by a recovery pass.

Cleared agent histories keep the last 5 sessions of raw messages detached from the prompt (MESSAGE_RETAIN_LAST_N_SESSIONS) purely so the distiller and auto-dream can read transcripts; distilled transcripts are pruned after 30 days.

One consolidation pass over episodic, semantic and knowledge vault together, merging cross-type duplicates; a dream checkpoint is written as a system episodic event and embedding vectors are stripped from the payload.
Memory agents get check_episodic_memory / check_semantic_memory to fetch full rows by ID, the counterpart of the summary-only prompt listing.
Optional LangFuse tracing creates one span per REST call and a child span per typed memory agent, so fan-out cost and latency are attributable per memory type.
Runners for RULER, LRU and LongMemEval-S with a sentence-aware 4,096-token chunker aligned to the official MAB settings, plus substring and LLM judges.

token_economy.t: Six mechanisms: (1) topic extraction compresses the conversation to a short ';'-separated keyword string before retrieval; (2) each typed list is capped at 10 items (MAX_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT_IN_SYSTEM) and episodic rows are shown as timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)', so verbose details are fetched only on demand via check tools; (3) procedural skills are never broadcast into prompts, only fetched by search; (4) memory agents' chat history is wiped after each update and agent context is summarised at 75% pressure down to 10% (keep last 5); (5) 'task' sessions skip inline extraction entirely; (6) the experience distiller caps each transcript at 80,000 chars (head+tail) and each turn at 8,000. Core blocks are capped at 5,000 chars each and always injected. Paper storage claim: 15.89 MB SQLite versus 15.07 GB raw screenshots (99.9% less). No tokens-per-question figure published.

speed.t: Async-native stack (asyncpg, redis.asyncio, aiokafka, httpx). Write is queued and returns immediately; sub-agents for different memory types run concurrently; worker pool partitioned by user_id hash (default 1 worker). Skill distillation runs fire-and-forget and distils sessions in parallel. /memory/search over all types runs concurrently and embeds the query once; /memory/retrieve/conversation is sequential and BM25-only. Optional Redis cache. Paper uses Gemini for async image upload. No latency numbers published on main; the graph_revision RESULTS.md reports 12.8 s/chunk ingest flat, 61.6 s with graph, and about 1 h QA for 1,540 questions.

keep: A cheap router call that picks which typed extractors run per batch, then runs them in parallel with small type-specific prompts and toolsets.
Active retrieval: one small-model call that outputs topics plus a temporal phrase, the phrase resolved to a date range by a rule-based parser, not the LLM.
Pointer-style context: show a summary plus details length, keep IDs only for the owning writer, and fetch details on demand.
Skills as a retrieval target, not ambient context, plus routing of task versus conversation sessions to different consolidation paths.
Neighbour-aware writes: each extractor sees the top-k existing rows of its own type with IDs, so it can merge or replace instead of appending.
avoid: Destructive LLM merges and replaces with no version history or link back to source turns; raw turns are not kept by default, so errors cannot be audited or re-derived.

Knowledge Vault stores credentials in a plain-text column, /memory/search returns secret_value unfiltered, the retrieve path skips scopes, and memory endpoints accept a bare x-client-id header without an API key.
Queued /memory/add returns before durability (in-process queue by default), and one failing sub-agent fails the whole fan-out.
Main's LoCoMo harness carries dataset-specific examples in its ingest and answer prompts (the vendor later flagged pre-August numbers as contaminated); the 4,096-d padding blocks ANN indexing.

specialities.name: Typed memory managers behind a router
specialities.t: A meta memory manager LLM picks which of five type-specialised agents (core, episodic, semantic, resource, knowledge vault) handle a batch, and they run concurrently, each with its own prompt and narrow tool set. Few engines split write-time extraction by memory type this way.

specialities.name: Pointer-style prompt context
specialities.t: Prompt listings show each event as timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)'; only the owning agent sees row IDs, and full details come through check tools on demand. This keeps neighbour context cheap without hiding that more text exists.

specialities.name: Adaptive task/conversation routing
specialities.t: A per-session session_tag sends tool-use 'task' sessions only to skill distillation (no inline extraction calls) and 'conversation' sessions only to typed extraction, so each kind of session pays for the memory it actually uses.

specialities.name: Budgeted skill self-evolution with lineage
specialities.t: Sealed sessions are distilled into worth_learning / worth_avoiding experiences with importance, credibility and an evidence quote; a curator then edits skills under a count-driven budget (max 6), a per-edit size gate (800 chars or 0.4 change ratio), semver patch bumps and soft-delete only, recording which experiences influenced which skills.

specialities.name: Exactly-once background trigger
specialities.t: The every-5-session procedural trigger is claimed through a persisted cursor row under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and dream runs hold a Postgres advisory lock, so multi-worker deployments neither double-fire nor skip a window.

specialities.name: LLM phrase, rule-based dates
specialities.t: Read-time topic extraction is a forced tool call returning topics and a temporal phrase; the phrase is turned into a date range by a deterministic parser rather than by the model, then filters episodic occurred_at.

specialities.name: Sensitivity-labelled knowledge vault
specialities.t: A dedicated store for credentials and reference values carries a low/medium/high sensitivity label; high items are withheld from every non-vault agent's prompt. The idea is unusual, though the column is unencrypted and search does not apply the filter.
